title: Dedicated autoscaler: smoother burst policy + utilization reporting
author: Ethan Miller
description: Context: Dedicated fleets experience short, high-amplitude spikes that cause large autoscaler oscillations and tail-latency regressions. This PR implements a smoother, token-bucket-based burst policy with an adaptive drain rate, improves fleet utilization reporting, and fixes a router backpressure corner-case during scale-up. Changes include: 1) New BurstController that manages burst credits per-fleet with an adaptive drain algorithm based on short-term EWMA of ingress and observed throughput; 2) Autoscaler tie-in to consider both long-term target replicas and short-term burst capacity to avoid unnecessary scale-ups; 3) New telemetry metrics: dedicated.autoscaler.burst_credit, dedicated.autoscaler.effective_throughput, dedicated.fleet.utilization_samp and per-replica burst distribution histograms; 4) Router backpressure fix to prevent queued request starvation when new instances come online; 5) Migration script and config flag (autoscaler.experimental_smoother_burst) to opt-in during rollout. Testing: unit tests for BurstController, integration tests for autoscaler decision loop, and end-to-end perf canary with synthetic spike traces. Rollout plan: canary on 5% of fleets for 48 hours, monitor burst_credit and tail latency, then 25% then 100%. Design doc: ENG-3421. Checklist: - design doc linked (ENG-3421) - unit + integration tests included - perf canary run and baselines collected - dashboards updated - rollout plan documented. Motivation and safety: smoother burst handling reduces churn and cost while keeping short spikes low-latency; conservative defaults keep behavior identical until flag enabled.
